macros.name: APACredefineOnce
macros.doc: This macro takes two arguments: (1) the name of a command (without the backslash) and (2) arbitrary TeX code. It then redefines the command (1) to the TeX code (2) as a one-time change, so after the command (1) has been invoked once, it reverts to its definition before \APACredefineOnce was issued.

macros.name: BAbstractRetrieved
macros.doc: This command is similar to \BRetrieved, except that it inserts “Abstract retrieved” instead of “Retrieved”.

macros.name: bibeditortype
macros.doc: The macro changes the definitions of the macros \BED and \BEDS to the argument and then immediately changes the definitions back to their old definitions.

macros.name: bibInstring
macros.doc: The macro changes the definition of the macro \BIn to the argument and then immediately changes the definition back to the old definition.

macros.name: bibleversion
macros.doc: This defines the version of the Bible used: \bibleversion{Revised Standard Version}.

macros.name: bibnodot
macros.doc: The \bibnodot command, defined in apacdoc.sty, swallows the period, so that there is no period after the URL in the reference list, thus complying with the APA rules.

macros.name: bibreftext
macros.doc: This command takes two arguments. By default, it ignores the first and inserts the second in the output.

macros.name: bibskipbracenodot
macros.doc: Suppresses the period after a subsequent closing brace.

macros.name: BmakeAbstractRetrieved
macros.doc: This command functions much like \bibeditortype: It replaces the next instance of \BRetrieved by \BAbstractRetrieved.

macros.name: noedition
macros.doc: Suppresses the “ed.” (or “\BEd”, rather) of an edition.

macros.name: swallowdot
macros.doc: Eats up the next character, but only if it’s a dot (‘.’).

macros.name: SwapArgs
macros.doc: This command takes two arguments and swaps their order.
